key_insight: GeoThinker-$F$ turns an MLLM’s own hidden states into predictive world representations, reducing dependence on external 3D encoders. This lets the model internalize spatial and temporal structure for faster, more efficient geometry-aware reasoning.
problem_solved: Geometry-aware MLLMs often need separate 3D encoder modules to inject spatial priors, which adds latency, memory cost, and inference complexity. The paper addresses how to preserve strong spatial intelligence without paying the overhead of extra encoder paths.
method: Transforms causal MLLM hidden states into endogenous latent world representations that carry spatiotemporal structure.
Uses predictive internal representations instead of external 3D feature extractors to support spatial reasoning.
Optimizes for efficiency by keeping perception and reasoning largely inside the main model pathway at inference time.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this offers a more deployment-friendly way to build spatially aware multimodal models with lower latency and compute. It is especially relevant for robotics, embodied AI, and real-time 3D understanding where speed matters.

paper_title: GeoThinker-$F$: Endogenous Predictive World Representations for Fast Spatial Intelligence
paper_authors: Haoyuan Li, Qihang Cao, Huanyuan Zhou, Xin Hu, Sijia Chen
